base_rich.content:
The overclock adds 50 MHz:

**Core clock**

| Item | Value (MHz) | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 4700 | [bench.example](https://bench.example/cpu-review) |
| Overclocked | 4750 | [bench.example](https://bench.example/cpu-review) |

Basis: measured. Scale: 0 to 4750 MHz.

at a higher voltage:

**Core voltage**

| Item | Value (V) | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 1.25 | [bench.example](https://bench.example/cpu-review) |
| Overclocked | 1.32 | [bench.example](https://bench.example/cpu-review) |

Basis: measured. Scale: 0 to 1.32 V.

If FPS tracked clock exactly:

**Average FPS (teaching example)**

| Item | Value (FPS) |
| --- | --- |
| Stock | 100 |
| Overclocked | 101 |

Basis: calculated — Assumes FPS scales exactly with core clock (about +1%); real games rarely scale this way. Scale: 0 to 101 FPS.

That is about 1%, within run-to-run noise.
